alert.raw: CRITICAL: Process injection into lsass.exe detected. Credential dumping tool signature (mimikatz) identified. Subsequent PsExec lateral movement to CORP-SRV-DC01 and CORP-SRV-FS02. Active C2 beacon to 185.220.101.47:443.

telemetry.detail: Unknown process (PID 4821, path: C:\Users\jsmith\AppData\Local\Temp\svchost32.exe) opened PROCESS_VM_READ handle to lsass.exe (PID 652)
EDR telemetry: sekurlsa::logonpasswords pattern matched; 3 NTLM hashes and 1 Kerberos TGT extracted from memory
PsExec.exe (SHA256: a3f2c9e...b99d) copied to \\CORP-SRV-DC01\admin$; remote service PSEXESVC created and started
PsExec.exe copied to \\CORP-SRV-FS02\admin$; remote service PSEXESVC created and started
HTTPS POST to 185.220.101.47:443 every 60s; jitter 10%; TLS fingerprint matches Cobalt Strike default malleable C2 profile

cachedVerdict.reasoning: Multiple high-confidence indicators confirm an active credential theft and lateral movement attack in progress. LSASS memory access by an unsigned binary dropped to a temp directory is a textbook Mimikatz execution pattern — no legitimate software writes to LSASS from AppData\Local\Temp. The extracted NTLM hashes were immediately leveraged via PsExec to pivot to two critical servers (domain controller and file server). The Cobalt Strike C2 beacon with a default malleable profile on a known malicious IP confirms a human operator is actively controlling the session. This is not a false positive — it is an active intrusion requiring immediate containment.

timeline.significance: Base64 encoding obscures payload — evasion tactic indicating deliberate obfuscation

timeline.event: LSASS memory access from temp-dir binary
timeline.significance: Critical: active credential theft; no legitimate software has this behavior pattern
Attacker now holds cryptographic credentials valid without knowing plaintext passwords

timeline.event: PsExec lateral movement to domain controller
timeline.significance: Domain controller compromised — maximum blast radius; all domain accounts at risk

timeline.event: PsExec lateral movement to file server
timeline.significance: Data exfiltration risk from FS02 — likely target for ransomware staging
Human operator in the loop — dwell time will accelerate without immediate response

evidence.signal: LSASS memory access by unsigned temp-dir binary (svchost32.exe)
evidence.why_it_matters: Standard Mimikatz execution pattern — LSASS holds all active domain credentials including Kerberos tickets
Attacker can perform pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket attacks against any resource these accounts can access
Domain controller access = keys to the kingdom; attacker can create accounts, change group policies, and achieve full domain dominance

evidence.signal: Cobalt Strike C2 beacon to 185.220.101.47 (known malicious IP)
evidence.why_it_matters: Active human operator controlling the session; threat will escalate rapidly without containment

containment.rationale: Cut C2 channel and prevent further lateral movement from patient zero while preserving for forensics

containment.action: Force password reset and revoke all active sessions
containment.rationale: Attacker holds jsmith NTLM hash; password reset invalidates the hash without needing plaintext recovery
Sever operator control channel across all potentially infected hosts on the network
PsExec may have deployed persistence mechanisms; audit before any remediation destroys forensic evidence

containment.action: Preserve full disk image before any remediation
containment.rationale: Chain-of-custody forensic image needed to determine initial access vector and legal/regulatory obligations

next_steps.step: Golden Ticket creation using extracted Kerberos TGT for domain-wide persistence
Ransomware deployment across all domain-joined systems via PsExec
Mass data exfiltration from CORP-SRV-FS02 file shares prior to encryption

cachedVerdict.ciso_summary: An attacker has stolen employee login credentials from one of our office computers and has already used them to reach the server that controls all company accounts and systems. If we do not act immediately, the attacker could disable every employee's access, deploy ransomware that encrypts all company data, or steal confidential files from our servers. We are isolating the affected computers, resetting the compromised credentials, and cutting off the attacker's remote control connection right now.
cachedVerdict.summary: Active intrusion: Mimikatz credential dump from CORP-WS-114 with PsExec lateral movement to domain controller and file server — Cobalt Strike C2 operator live. Isolate WS-114, reset jsmith, block C2 IP now.
